newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Acacia to expand Union Reefs mine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Acacia to expand Union Reefs mine.

text.p: Acacia Resources Ltd said on Monday it will spend A$14.2 million to expand its Union Reefs gold mine in the Northern Territory.
Gold production would be increased to about 120,000 ounces in 1998, compared with 87,000 ounces produced in 1996, the company said in a statement.
Acacia said exploration drilling had boosted resources at Union Reefs to 1.3 million ounces. Reserves are 0.6 million ounces.
Managing director Michael Folie said the increase in resources had given the board confidence to lift throughput from 1.65 million tonnes a year to 2.1 million tonnes a year.
The expansion capital would be used to provide a tertiary crusher, an extra ball-mill and two leach tanks.
The Union Reefs mine, wholly owned by Acacia, is located 175 km southeast of Darwin in the Northern Territory.
The mine produced 172,000 ounces of gold at an average cash cost of A$362 an ounce in the two years to the end of 1996.
